test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 23 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In 2025, which state decided to review the Shakti Bill, which was to protect children and women from crime?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **2025**, the **Maharashtra** government decided to review and update the **Shakti Criminal Laws (Maharashtra Amendment) Bill**.
 
• The **Shakti Bill** was originally passed by the **Maharashtra State Legislature** in **December 2021**, following the outrage over several heinous crimes against **women and children**.
 
• The decision to review the bill in **2025** stems from the need to align its provisions with the new central criminal laws—the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)**, **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)**, and **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA)**—which replaced the **IPC** and **CrPC** in **July 2024**.
 
• The bill was modeled on the **Andhra Pradesh Disha Act** and aims to provide for the **death penalty** in cases of rape and gang rape, especially against children, and to speed up the judicial process.
 
• Because the bill seeks to amend criminal law (a **Concurrent List** subject), it requires **Presidential assent**; the **2025** review ensures that the amendments remain legally viable under the new **National Criminal Code** framework.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Scope of Punishment**:
 
 
• The **Shakti Bill** proposes the **death penalty** or **life imprisonment** for the remainder of the natural life of the convict in cases of **rape, gang rape, and sexual assault** against minors.
 
• It also introduces a provision for a fine of up to **Rs. 10 lakh** for the perpetrator, which would be utilized for the victim's **medical expenses** and **rehabilitation**.
 
 
 
• **Expedited Investigation and Trial**:
 
 
• The bill mandates that the **investigation** of such crimes be completed within **15 working days** (extendable to 30 days under specific circumstances).
 
• The **trial** is expected to be concluded within **30 working days** from the date of filing the charge sheet, ensuring **swift justice** for the victims.
 
 
 
• **Special Units and Courts**:
 
 
• It proposes the establishment of **Special Police Teams** and **Special Courts** in each district of **Maharashtra** to handle cases related to the safety of **women and children**.
 
• The bill also addresses **cybercrimes**, proposing strict action against those who harass women via **social media** or digital platforms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legal Necessity**: The **2025** review is critical because many sections of the **IPC** and **CrPC** cited in the original **2021** draft no longer exist. Ensuring "concordance" with the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)** is necessary for the bill to be enforceable once it receives the **President's signature**.
 
• **Joint Select Committee**: The draft of the bill had previously undergone rigorous scrutiny by a **Joint Select Committee** of the **Maharashtra State Legislature** before its initial passage to balance the rights of the accused with the safety of women.
 
• **Constitutional Framework**: Under **Article 254(2)** of the **Constitution of India**, a state law on a **Concurrent List** subject can override a central law only if it receives **Presidential assent**, making the current alignment process vital for **Maharashtra**.
